mainTopic: Examining new-moon witnesses, the declaration of 'מקודש', and רבן גמליאל's moon diagrams
overview: This amud opens with the last words of the rainbow discussion from the previous page. The גמרא then returns to the questions put to the witnesses of the new moon. Two ברייתות disagree about whether the moon appears north or south of the sun, and the גמרא explains that one is about summer and the other about winter. Further ברייתות teach how much witnesses may disagree about the moon's height. They also teach that a reflection, a view through clouds, or a sighting the witnesses could not find again on purpose is not valid testimony. A new משנה describes the ראש בית דין declaring 'מקודש' and the people answering 'מקודש מקודש', and the גמרא brings a פסוק for each part. Three תנאים disagree about when the month is declared, and שמואל rules like רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק. A further משנה tells how רבן גמליאל used pictures of the moon to question witnesses. The גמרא asks whether such images are allowed, and אביי answers that only attendants humans can reproduce are forbidden, supporting this with a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the rainbow discussion: so no one says the sun shoots arrows
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the previous discussion. The rainbow is turned away from the sun so that sun-worshippers cannot say the sun is shooting arrows at its enemies.
steps.simpleTranslation: [So that the sun-worshippers should not say that the sun] is shooting arrows.
steps.whatsHappening: This short line finishes a discussion that began on the previous page. The rainbow is shaped so that it never looks like a bow held by the sun, and this line gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous lines asked why the curve of the rainbow faces away from the sun. The answer ends here: if the bow faced the sun, idol-worshippers of the sun would say the sun is shooting arrows at people who reject it. This closes that side topic, and the גמרא now goes back to the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: arrows
is shooting / throwing

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the end of a sentence that started on the previous page (23b), so do not read it alone.

phrases.english: [the sun] is shooting arrows.
phrases.notes: End of the sentence: 'so that sun-worshippers should not say the sun is shooting arrows.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a side discussion from the previous daf about the rainbow.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rainbow faces away from the sun so that it never looks like the sun is shooting arrows.

steps.title: A teaching on direction: the moon must be north of the sun
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's questions about the moon's height and direction. It then brings a ברייתא: a witness who says the moon was north of the sun is believed, and one who says south has said nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'How high was it, and to which side was it leaning, etc.' It was taught in one ברייתא: If he says it was to the north of the sun, his words stand. If he says to the south, he has said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's questions for the witnesses and quotes a ברייתא that explains the 'direction' question. This also sets up the next step, where a second ברייתא will seem to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new moon appears near the sun, on one particular side of it. A true witness would report the correct side. A witness who reports the impossible side shows that he did not really see the moon, so his testimony is worthless.

keyTerms.meaning: how high was it (the moon above the horizon)
to which side was it leaning
it was taught in one ברייתא
his words stand (his testimony is valid)
he has said nothing (his testimony is worthless)

phrases.english: How high was it,
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה: a question put to the witnesses.

phrases.english: and to which side was it leaning, etc.
It was taught in one baraita:
if he says to its north, his words stand,
phrases.notes: 'Its' means the sun's: the moon was north of the sun.

phrases.english: if he says to its south, he has said nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּמָּה הָיָה גָּבוֹהַּ, וּלְאַיִן הָיָה נוֹטֶה כּוּ׳. תָּנָא חֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the rainbow topic and returns to the משנה about examining the witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A witness who places the moon north of the sun is believed. One who places it south is not.

steps.title: A contradicting teaching: the moon must be south of the sun
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a second ברייתא that says the exact opposite: south is valid and north is worthless.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught the opposite in another ברייתא: If he says to the south, his words stand. If he says to the north, he has said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first ברייתא with a second ברייתא that reverses it. Now we have two sources that cannot both seem true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות use the same wording, but they swap north and south. Either one source is wrong, or each one is talking about a different situation. The next step will explain which.

keyTerms.meaning: but it was taught (in a ברייתא), introducing a contradiction
the opposite

phrases.english: But it was taught the opposite:
if he says to its south, his words stand,
if he says to its north, he has said nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the ברייתא quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of the first ברייתא that north is valid and south is invalid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא of equal authority says the reverse, so the two sources seem to contradict each other.

steps.title: Resolution: one teaching is about summer, the other about winter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says there is no real contradiction. The moon's position relative to the sun changes with the seasons, so each ברייתא is describing a different time of year.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it is talking about the summer, and there it is talking about the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by explaining that each ברייתא describes a different season. Both are correct, each for its own time of year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the summer the sun travels in the northern part of the sky, so the new moon appears to its south. That matches the second ברייתא. In the winter (the rainy season) the sun is in the south, so the moon appears to its north. That matches the first ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (there is no contradiction)
here (this source)
the summer months
the rainy season (winter)

steps.whatToRemember: The 'correct' direction of the moon depends on the season: south of the sun in summer, north of the sun in winter. A witness whose report fits the season is believed.
steps.confusionAlert: The text just says 'here' and 'here' without saying which ברייתא is which. Summer goes with the 'south' ברייתא (step 3), and winter goes with the 'north' ברייתא (step 2).

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, in the summer.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא that says south is valid.

phrases.english: here, in the rainy season.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא that says north is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן, בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה. כָּאן, בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source applies to a different season.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות disagree about the same situation.
steps.terutzMaskana: They describe different seasons, and both are correct.

steps.title: How much witnesses may disagree about the moon's height
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a small disagreement about the moon's height (two versus three) is acceptable, but a large one (three versus five) cancels the testimony. Even so, each witness may still join with a different witness who agrees with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If one says it was two ox-goads high and the other says three, their testimony stands. If one says three and the other says five, their testimony is cancelled. But they may join with another testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the משנה's question 'how high was it' and sets the limits for disagreement between witnesses about the height.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A difference of one unit is a normal estimating error, so the witnesses still count as agreeing. A difference of two units means they do not agree, so the pair cannot be accepted together. However, neither witness is called a liar. Each one may pair up with another witness whose report matches his.

keyTerms.meaning: the רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)
ox-goads (Sefaria: plow handles), used as a unit for estimating height
their testimony stands
their testimony is cancelled
they join together (combine to make a pair of witnesses)

steps.whatToRemember: A small disagreement (one unit) is tolerated. A larger one (two units) cancels the pair's testimony, but it does not disqualify the witnesses themselves.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Their testimony is cancelled' does not mean the witnesses are liars or are disqualified. Only this particular pairing fails, and each one may still testify together with someone else who agrees with him.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the difference between rejecting a testimony and rejecting the witness. A disagreement may break the pairing without making either person an invalid witness.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
if one says it was two ox-goads high,
and the other says three,
their testimony stands.
phrases.notes: A small difference is a normal estimating error.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר שָׁלֹשׁ, וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר חָמֵשׁ —
phrases.english: If one says three and the other says five,
their testimony is cancelled.
phrases.notes: The difference is too large for them to count as agreeing.

phrases.english: But they may join with another testimony.
phrases.notes: Each witness may pair with a different witness who agrees with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר גָּבוֹהַּ שְׁתֵּי מַרְדְּעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the 'direction' question to the 'height' question of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A one-unit disagreement about height is acceptable. A two-unit disagreement cancels the pair's testimony, but each witness may still combine with another matching witness.

steps.title: A reflection or a sighting through clouds is not valid
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that witnesses who saw the moon in water, in a glass lantern, or through clouds cannot testify. The same applies if they saw half of it that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If witnesses say 'We saw it in water,' 'We saw it in a glass lantern,' or 'We saw it in the clouds,' they may not testify about it. If they say half in water, half in clouds, or half in a lantern, they may not testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about which kinds of moon sightings are not good enough for עדות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testimony about the new moon needs a direct look at the moon in the sky. A reflection in water or a glass, or a blurry view through clouds, is not a real sighting. The ברייתא then adds a line about 'half', which the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)
A glass lantern or glass pane
Clouds
They may not testify about it

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'We saw it in the water,'
'We saw it in a glass lantern,'
'We saw it through the clouds'
they may not testify about it.
Half of it in the water, half of it through the clouds,
half of it in a lantern
they may not testify about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the moon's position and height to a new topic: how the moon must be seen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a direct sighting of the moon is valid. A reflection, or a view through glass or clouds, cannot be used for testimony.

steps.title: Why teach half if the whole is already invalid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to say 'half' is invalid. If seeing the whole moon this way does not count, then seeing only half obviously does not count either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if about the whole moon you said it is not valid, is it even necessary to say that half is not valid?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא, saying the second half of it seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is about extra words. If a full reflection is not valid, a half reflection is clearly worse, so the ברייתא should not need to teach it. This pushes the גמרא to find a new meaning for the 'half' line.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (opens an 'if this, then surely that' argument)
All of it, the whole moon
Is it necessary [to say]?

phrases.english: Now, about all of it you said 'no',
is it necessary to say so about half of it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא כּוּלּוֹ אָמְרַתְּ לָא, חֶצְיוֹ מִבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second clause of the ברייתא in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The clause about half in water, clouds, or lantern.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the whole moon seen indirectly is invalid, half seen indirectly is obviously invalid too, so the clause adds nothing.

steps.title: Half reflected and half seen directly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא means half the moon was seen indirectly and the other half directly in the sky. Even that does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it is saying: half in water and half in the sky, half in clouds and half in the sky, half in a lantern and half in the sky, they may not testify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by reading the 'half' clause in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'half' line is not about seeing only half the moon. It describes a mixed view, where part was seen directly in the sky and part was seen indirectly. Without this line, we might think seeing half of it directly is good enough, so the ברייתא teaches that the whole moon must be seen directly.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what it means (re-reads a source)
The sky
Half of it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'half in water' as seeing only half the moon. The גמרא explains it as half reflected and the other half seen directly. The point is that a partly direct view is still not enough.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it is saying:
half of it in the water and half of it in the sky,
half of it through the clouds and half of it in the sky,
half of it in a lantern and half of it in the sky
they may not testify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 7 by re-reading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-interpretation of the ברייתא's wording (הכי קאמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'half' clause means only half the moon was seen, all of it indirectly, which would make it a pointless repeat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clause means half was seen indirectly and half directly. It teaches that the entire moon must be seen directly in the sky.
steps.whatToRemember: For valid testimony, the whole moon must be seen directly in the sky. A mixed view of half direct and half reflected is not enough.

steps.title: Saw it once and not again
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא teaches that if the witnesses saw the moon but did not see it again, they cannot testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If they say 'We saw it, and then we did not see it again,' they may not testify about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second new ברייתא about a sighting that could not be repeated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance, the ברייתא seems to say that a single glimpse is not enough. That sounds strange, and the גמרא will question it next.

keyTerms.meaning: We saw it
And we did not see it again

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'We saw it, and then we did not see it again'
they may not testify about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: רְאִינוּהוּ וְשׁוּב לֹא רְאִינוּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא on another kind of doubtful sighting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who saw the moon and then did not see it again cannot testify.

steps.title: Must they keep watching the moon the whole time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that witnesses should not have to keep looking at the moon. One clear sighting should be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Must they keep on watching it all that time?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא, because demanding a second sighting seems unreasonable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testimony is about seeing the new moon, and nowhere is there a rule that you must keep watching it. A thin new moon often disappears quickly, so the ruling seems too strict. The גמרא needs to find a case where the ruling makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: All that much, to such an extent
They see / watch
And keep going (continuing to do it)

phrases.english: Must they keep watching it to such an extent?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the ברייתא in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that 'we saw it and did not see it again' disqualifies the testimony.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no reason to require continued watching. One real sighting should be enough.

steps.title: They searched again on purpose and found nothing
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the case: they saw it by chance, then looked for it on purpose and could not find it. Maybe what they saw was only a small round cloud.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, this is what it means: 'We saw it on our own, and we went back to look at it on purpose, and we did not see it.' They may not testify about it. What is the reason? Say that it was merely a small round cloud that they saw.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by describing the exact case the ברייתא is talking about, and gives the reason for the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not that the moon disappeared over time. The witnesses deliberately searched the same spot right away and found nothing, which raises real doubt about the first sighting. Since the moon should still have been there, what they first saw was probably a small white cloud that looked like the moon.

keyTerms.meaning: On our own, by chance, without looking for it
On purpose, deliberately
What is the reason?
Say, one could suggest
A small round cloud

steps.whatToRemember: A sighting is doubted only when the witnesses looked for the moon again on purpose and could not find it. Then we worry they saw a small cloud and not the moon.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that בית דין tests the reliability of a sighting. The concern is not how long the moon was seen, but whether the witnesses could have mistaken something else for it.

phrases.english: Abaye said, this is what it is saying:
'We saw it on our own,'
'and we went back to look at it on purpose,'
'and we did not see it'
they may not testify about it.
What is the reason?
Say that a small round cloud
is merely what they saw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 10 by defining the case of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-interpretation of the ברייתא by narrowing the case (הכי קאמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא requires witnesses to keep watching the moon continuously.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers to witnesses who searched again on purpose and failed to find it. This makes us suspect they saw a cloud.

steps.title: The משנה: the court head declares 'sanctified' and the people answer
steps.stepSummary: The ראש בית דין says 'מקודש', the people answer 'מקודש מקודש', and the month is declared whether or not the moon was seen on time.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The head of the court says, 'It is sanctified!' All the people answer after him, 'It is sanctified! It is sanctified!' Whether the moon was seen at its proper time or not, the court sanctifies the month.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes the ceremony that happens after the עדים are accepted: the ראש בית דין formally declares the new month, and everyone answers him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the sugya was about how the עדים see the moon and how they are checked. Now the משנה moves to the official declaration itself. The תנא קמא holds that the declaration is said in every case, even when the moon was not seen at its expected time.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; the start of the משנה text
The head of the court
'It is sanctified', the official declaration of the new month
At its time, meaning the moon was seen on the expected day
They sanctify, meaning they formally declare the month

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not seen at its time' does not mean the month is never set. It means the moon was not seen on the 30th day, so the next day becomes ראש חודש automatically. The only question is whether the court still says 'מקודש' on that day.

phrases.english: MISHNAH
The head of the court says: 'Sanctified!'
and all the people respond after him:
'Sanctified! Sanctified!'
Whether it was seen at its time,
or whether it was not seen at its time,
they sanctify it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It moves from checking the witnesses to the formal declaration of the month.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ראש בית דין declares 'מקודש' and the people answer twice. According to the תנא קמא, this is done whether or not the moon was seen on time.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר son of רבי צדוק: no declaration if the moon was not seen on time
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק holds that if the moon was not seen on time, the court does not declare, because Heaven already sanctified the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר son of רבי צדוק says: If the moon was not seen at its time, they do not sanctify it, because Heaven has already sanctified it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the משנה disagrees with the first. When the moon was not seen on time, this opinion says there is no declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the moon is not seen on the 30th, the next day is ראש חודש no matter what, since a month cannot be longer than 30 days. רבי אלעזר says the court's declaration would add nothing here, because 'Heaven' (the fixed natural order) already set the day. The תנא קמא holds that the court declares anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי אלעזר son of רבי צדוק, a תנא
Heaven has already sanctified it

steps.whyThisMatters: This argument shows what the court's declaration is for. Either it is always part of making the month, or it is needed only when the court actually decides which day is ראש חודש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says:
If it was not seen at its time,
they do not sanctify it,
for Heaven has already sanctified it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא about the case where the moon was not seen on time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the moon was not seen on time, the court does not say 'מקודש', because Heaven already fixed the day.

steps.title: Source question: where do we learn that the court head declares?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks for the source that the ראש בית דין must say 'מקודש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה said, 'The head of the court…' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the start of the משנה and asks where the rule comes from. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the משנה. It is a request for the פסוק behind the practice of a formal declaration by the ראש בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Etc.; the quote is cut short
From where are these matters derived?

phrases.english: GEMARA
'The head of the court…' etc.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the first clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches the ראש בית דין must declare 'מקודש'.

steps.title: Source: 'And משה declared the appointed seasons of ה׳'
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of tradition back to רבי, the פסוק 'וידבר משה את מועדי ה׳' teaches that the ראש בית דין declares 'מקודש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר גמדא said in the name of רבי יוסי בן שאול, who said in the name of רבי: The פסוק says, 'And משה declared the appointed seasons of ה׳.' From here we learn that the head of the court says 'Sanctified.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק about משה announcing the מועדים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was the head of the highest court of his time. Since he 'spoke' (declared) the מועדים, the head of the court in each generation also declares the new month out loud.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who passes on this teaching
The פסוק says
The appointed seasons of ה׳
From here we learn

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Gamda said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן שָׁאוּל אָמַר רַבִּי:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yosei ben Shaul said that Rabbi said:
The verse says:
'And Moses declared the appointed seasons of the Lord'
From here we learn that the head of the court says 'Sanctified.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא ״וַיְדַבֵּר מֹשֶׁה אֶת מוֹעֲדֵי ה׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה, the head of the court, declared the מועדים. So the ראש בית דין declares the new month.

steps.title: Source question: where do we learn that the people answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה and asks for the source that all the people answer 'מקודש מקודש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said, 'And all the people answer after him, Sanctified! Sanctified!' From where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second part of the משנה and asks for its source. The answers come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק only showed that the leader declares. A new source is needed to show that the whole nation also takes part.

keyTerms.meaning: They respond after him
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: 'And all the people respond after him
Sanctified! Sanctified!'
From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first clause of the משנה to the second.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches the people must answer 'מקודש מקודש'.

steps.title: רב פפא: read אותם as אתם (you)
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reads the word 'אותם' in the פסוק as 'אתם' (you), teaching that the people themselves also proclaim the month.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The פסוק says, 'which you shall proclaim them (אותם).' Read it as 'you (אתם)'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the first answer. He uses a word in the פסוק that can be read in a second way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אותם ('them') is written without a ו, so it can also be read אַתֶּם ('you'). That reading means 'you shall proclaim', so the people also take part in proclaiming the מועדים by answering.

keyTerms.meaning: רב פפא, an אמורא
You shall proclaim
Read into it; read the word in a different way
You (plural)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The verse states: 'Which you shall proclaim them'
Read it as 'you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Reading אותם as אתם teaches that 'you', the people, also proclaim.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: 'they' shall say 'My appointed seasons'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק learns the same rule from 'אלה הם מועדי': 'they' (the people) shall say the מועדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The פסוק says, 'These are (הם) My appointed seasons.' Read it as: 'they' shall say My appointed seasons.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different פסוק for the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הם seems extra in the sentence. רב נחמן בר יצחק reads it as 'they', meaning the people, who must also say the מועדים. The rule is the same as רב פפא's; only the source is different.

keyTerms.meaning: רב נחמן בר יצחק, an אמורא
They; here, the people
My appointed seasons

steps.whatToRemember: The ראש בית דין declares 'מקודש', based on 'וידבר משה'. The people answer 'מקודש מקודש', based on 'אתם' (רב פפא) or 'הם' (רב נחמן בר יצחק). The two אמוראים agree on the rule and differ only on which פסוק teaches it.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
'These are My appointed seasons'
'They' shall say My appointed seasons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate source for the same rule as step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word הם means 'they', so the people also declare the מועדים.

steps.title: Why do the people say 'Sanctified' twice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the people must repeat 'מקודש' two times.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need them to say 'Sanctified, sanctified' two times?
steps.whatsHappening: We just learned that the people answer the ראש בית דין. Now the גמרא notices that the משנה has them say 'מקודש' twice, and asks why one time is not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 17-18 explained why the people speak at all. This question is narrower. It asks about the doubling of the word, which also needs a source.

keyTerms.meaning: Two times
Why do I need it? (asking for the reason or source of a detail)

phrases.english: "Sanctified, sanctified" two times
why do I need this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the analysis of the people's response by asking about its doubled wording.

steps.title: The plural 'convocations' teaches saying it twice
steps.stepSummary: The plural word 'מקראי' in the פסוק 'מקראי קודש' teaches that the declaration is said twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written 'sacred convocations' (plural).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק says 'מקראי קודש' in the plural. That plural means the announcement is made twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מקראי' is a plural form, meaning 'callings' or 'proclamations.' The smallest plural is two, so the people call out 'מקודש' two times.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacred convocations, or holy proclamations (plural)
For it is written

steps.whatToRemember: The ראש בית דין says 'מקודש' once. All the people answer 'מקודש מקודש' twice, because of the plural 'מקראי'.

phrases.english: Because it is written: "Sacred convocations" (plural).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר son of רבי צדוק: no declaration if the moon was not seen on time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if the moon was not seen at its time, בית דין does not declare 'מקודש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר son of רבי צדוק says: If the moon was not seen at its expected time, we do not declare it sanctified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes the next part of the משנה, the opinion of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק, to start discussing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The expected time is the 30th day. If the moon was not seen then, ראש חודש falls automatically on day 31. Since that day comes on its own, בית דין does not need to declare 'מקודש'.

keyTerms.meaning: At its proper or expected time (here, the 30th day)
We do not sanctify it (בית דין does not formally declare 'מקודש')
The תנא whose opinion in the משנה is being discussed

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not sanctified' does NOT mean there is no ראש חודש. ראש חודש still happens on day 31. Only the formal declaration of 'מקודש' is skipped.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says:
If it was not seen at its time,
we do not sanctify it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, separate from the wording of the declaration.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the moon was not seen on day 30, ראש חודש on day 31 is not formally declared 'מקודש'.

steps.title: פלימו: the reverse view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes פלימו, who holds that a month arriving at its time is not sanctified, but one arriving not at its time is.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: פלימו says: At its time, we do not sanctify it. Not at its time, we do sanctify it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a different opinion. פלימו flips the rule: a month that comes at its normal time needs no declaration, but one that comes at an unusual time does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פלימו reasons that a month arriving as expected is already fixed by its natural timing, so no declaration is needed. When the month arrives at an unexpected time, a formal declaration is needed to establish it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
פלימו, a תנא
Not at its expected time

phrases.english: It was taught: Palaimo says:
At its time, we do not sanctify it;
not at its time, we do sanctify it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an opposing opinion to רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A month on its natural schedule needs no declaration. An irregular one does.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון: months are never formally sanctified
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds there is no formal declaration of 'מקודש' in either case. He learns this from 'וקדשתם את שנת החמשים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון says: In either case we do not sanctify it, as it says 'And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year.' Years you sanctify, but months you do not sanctify.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא gives a third opinion. Months never get a formal 'מקודש' declaration, and he brings a פסוק to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about יובל says to sanctify 'the year.' He reads this as limiting formal sanctification to years only. Months are sanctified by Heaven on their own, so בית דין only needs to announce the date.

keyTerms.meaning: Either way, in both cases
'And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year' (the יובל year)
Years and months

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין אוֹתוֹ,
phrases.english: Either way, we do not sanctify it,
as it is stated: "And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year":
years you sanctify,
but you do not sanctify months.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion in the same ברייתא, rejecting the formal declaration entirely.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only years require formal sanctification. Months never do.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר son of רבי צדוק
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules like רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק: declare 'מקודש' when the moon is seen on time, but not when it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is like רבי אלעזר son of רבי צדוק.
steps.whatsHappening: After three opinions, the גמרא gives the practical ruling. We follow the view in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the מחלוקת. When the moon is seen on day 30, בית דין declares 'מקודש'. When ראש חודש falls automatically on day 31, it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the view of...
רב יהודה quoting his teacher שמואל

steps.whatToRemember: Three views: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק (declare only on day 30), פלימו (the reverse), and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון (never declare). The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is like Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides among the opinions just presented.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Declare 'מקודש' only when the new month starts on day 30.

steps.title: אביי's support from a משנה: 'full' yes, 'sanctified' no
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a משנה: if night fell before בית דין could declare 'מקודש', the month becomes full. It then gets no declaration, which supports רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We also learned this in a משנה. If בית דין and all Israel saw the moon, and the witnesses were questioned, but they did not manage to say 'Sanctified' before it got dark, the month is made full. 'Full' — yes. 'Sanctified' — no.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי says this ruling can already be found in a משנה. He shows that when the new month ends up falling on day 31, the משנה mentions no declaration of 'מקודש'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's case, day 30 ended without a declaration, so the old month became full and ראש חודש moved to day 31. The משנה only says 'it is full' and never says to declare day 31 'מקודש'. This matches רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק: a day-31 ראש חודש is not formally sanctified.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned this (in a משנה); introduces supporting proof
The witnesses were questioned
Until it became dark
Made full, the previous month gets 30 days
Yes... no (a precise inference from the wording)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the ruling of שמואל is already built into an anonymous משנה, so it is not just one תנא's view.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Abaye said: We too have learned:
If the court and all Israel saw it,
the witnesses were interrogated,
but they did not manage to say "Sanctified" before it grew dark,
this month is made full.
Full — yes; sanctified — no.
phrases.notes: The inference: no 'מקודש' declaration for a day-31 ראש חודש.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's ruling with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that a day-31 ראש חודש is not declared 'מקודש' (רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording 'הרי זה מעובר', which mentions no declaration of 'מקודש'.

steps.title: The משנה only needed to teach that the month becomes full
steps.stepSummary: The proof from the night-fall משנה is rejected. The משנה's point is that the month becomes מעובר even though everyone saw the moon. It says nothing about whether 'מקודש' is declared.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה needed to tell us that the month becomes full (מעובר). You might have thought: since בית דין and all of Israel saw the moon, it is public knowledge, so we should not make the month full. The משנה teaches us that we still do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's proof from Step 25. The משנה had a different reason for saying the month becomes full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי read the משנה's phrase 'the month is מעובר' as a hint that no 'מקודש' is said. The גמרא answers that the phrase is there to block a mistake. Someone might think that a moon seen by everyone is so well known that the month should start right away, even without a formal declaration. The משנה is teaching that rule, so it tells us nothing either way about saying 'מקודש' on the next day.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed for him; the statement had a purpose
It might have entered your mind to say (sets up a mistaken assumption)
It became publicized, publicly known
It teaches us (the new point the source adds)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not prove that 'מקודש' IS said in that case. It only shows that the משנה cannot be used as a proof. שמואל's ruling in step 24, like רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק, still stands.

phrases.english: It was necessary for him to say 'full (extended)',
since it might enter your mind to say:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְרָאוּהוּ בֵּית דִּין וְכׇל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: since the court and all of Israel saw it,
it has become public, so they should not make it full,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proof by giving the משנה's wording a different purpose.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not reject שמואל's ruling or רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק's view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'מעובר' is needed for its own teaching: a publicly seen moon still does not cancel the extension of the month. So it cannot hint at the absence of 'מקודש'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The night-fall משנה gives no proof about the declaration of 'מקודש'.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's diagrams of the moon's shapes
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: רבן גמליאל had pictures of the moon's phases. He used them to help simple witnesses describe what they saw.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל had pictures of the shapes of the moon on a tablet on the wall of his upper room. He would show them to ordinary people and ask: 'Did you see it like this, or like this?'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes a tool רבן גמליאל used when he questioned witnesses about the new moon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simple witnesses often cannot describe the crescent clearly in words. The pictures let בית דין check that the witness's description matches what is really possible, such as the direction of the crescent and its size. This sets up the גמרא's question about whether making such pictures is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Images of the shapes (phases) of the moon
A tablet or board
Upper story, attic room
Ordinary or unlearned people

phrases.english: MISHNA: Images of the forms of the moon
Rabban Gamliel had
on a tablet on the wall of his upper room,
with which he would show the ordinary people,
and he would say: Did you see it like this, or like this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ דְּמוּת צוּרוֹת לְבָנָה הָיוּ לוֹ לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The topic shifts from saying 'מקודש' to how witnesses are examined.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל used pictures of the moon's phases to examine witnesses.

steps.title: Isn't it forbidden to make images of the heavenly bodies?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבן גמליאל could make moon pictures. The פסוק 'לא תעשון אתי' is read as forbidding images of God's 'attendants'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this allowed? But it is written: 'You shall not make with Me', which means: do not make images of My attendants (the sun, moon, and so on).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. Making a picture of the moon seems to break a Torah איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דרשה reads 'אתי' (with Me) as referring to those who are 'with' God, meaning the beings that serve before Him, which include the heavenly bodies. The moon is one of these 'attendants', so a picture of it should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it permitted? (opens a challenge)
But isn't it written? (brings a פסוק against the case)
My attendants: the heavenly bodies that serve God

phrases.english: GEMARA: And is it permitted?
But isn't it written: 'You shall not make with Me' —
meaning: you shall not make the likeness of My attendants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the action described in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's practice of keeping drawings of the moon.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק forbids images of God's attendants. The moon is one of them, so drawing it should be forbidden.

steps.title: אביי: only reproducible attendants are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: אביי limits the איסור to attendants whose likeness can actually be reproduced. That excludes רבן גמליאל's moon drawings.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The Torah only forbade making images of attendants that it is possible to make like them.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. He narrows what the איסור includes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איסור does not cover every one of God's attendants. It covers only attendants that people are able to reproduce, such as the בית המקדש and its כלים. No person can ever make a sun or a moon, so the heavenly bodies fall outside the איסור, and רבן גמליאל's drawings are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah forbade only...
That it is possible to make like them (reproduce)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The Torah forbade only those attendants
that it is possible to make like them,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא שַׁמָּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by limiting the scope of the איסור.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the איסור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any image of a heavenly attendant is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only attendants that can truly be reproduced are included. The moon drawings fall outside the איסור.

steps.title: A ברייתא: do not copy the בית המקדש and its כלים exactly
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא forbids building exact copies of the היכל, אולם, עזרה, שלחן, and מנורה. It begins to list what is allowed, which supports אביי's 'reproducible' rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: A person may not build a house in the form of the היכל, a porch in the form of the אולם, a courtyard like the עזרה, a table like the שלחן, or a candelabrum like the מנורה. But one may make...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support אביי. Its list of allowed items continues past the end of this passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item in the ברייתא is something a person really can copy exactly, such as a building or a vessel. Those exact copies are forbidden. This matches אביי's idea that the איסור targets true reproductions. The words 'אבל עושה' show that some versions are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא (introduces support)
The exact form of the Sanctuary building
A portico or porch
The Temple courtyard
But one may make (opens the allowed cases)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the classic source for the הלכה that one may not make an exact copy of the בית המקדש or its כלים, such as a seven-branched מנורה.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם בַּיִת תַּבְנִית הֵיכָל,
phrases.english: A person may not make a house in the form of the Sanctuary,
a portico in the form of the Entrance Hall,
a courtyard corresponding to the Temple courtyard,
a table corresponding to the Temple table,
a candelabrum corresponding to the Temple candelabrum.
But one may make
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא: לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם בַּיִת תַּבְנִית הֵיכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to back up אביי's answer.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's rule that only reproducible attendants or holy objects are forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא forbidding exact copies of the בית המקדש and its כלים.
